articles.title: AI Video Generator Community
articles.author: Tiqua Jackson
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. A leafy square fills the screen. Tables sit in warm light, bicycles pass quietly, and every part of the proposed space seems settled. A resident who disagrees with the arrangement now has to argue against a finished-looking place. Yet the actual question may still be whether the square should favour seating, a market, or an open area for informal use. Community groups using an AI Video Generator can avoid that imbalance by showing alternatives with comparable treatment. A single polished vision tends to hide the choices that produced it. articles.title: Bloated Military Budget
articles.author: Matthew Hoh
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. The United States can always find money for war. But when Americans need healthcare, education, housing, or investments in their communities, the familiar refrain is that there simply isn't enough money. That contradiction framed Our Bloated Military Budget , a session at the 2026 Left Coast Forum, held October 2–4 at California State University, Los Angeles. Featuring military veteran and peace advocate Matthew Hoh and foreign policy analyst Ben Freeman , the discussion examined the human and moral consequences of American militarism and the political culture that allows it to continue. articles.title: What I Learned in Nagasaki
articles.author: Chuck Yates
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. One day in 1964, at the age of nineteen, I rode around Nagasaki on a tour bus with a Japanese friend. Profoundly ignorant of Japan, I was ill equipped to process the sights we saw—the broken ruins of Urakami Cathedral, near the hypocenter, and the peace park with its monumental statue sitting atop the hill, right hand pointing to the sky as if warning of danger from above, left hand extended palm down as if urging peace and harmony, eyes closed as if in prayer. Nor was I prepared for the city’s A-bomb museum. In one room, there was a section of the wooden outer wall of a building, unremarkable except for the human silhouette burned into it. articles.content_excerpt: A plaza just outside 780 Third Avenue in Midtown Manhattan, brimming with well-tended flowers in warm weather and furnished with elegant stone benches, looks like an inviting place to sit down and enjoy a slice of pizza. Or at least Wade Phillips certainly thought so. Phillips, a hospitality and security worker, used to take his breaks in that plaza every day. articles.title: Rabid Anti-Communism Still Shapes the Politics of California
articles.author: Michael G. Vann
articles.content_excerpt: Donald Trump’s political vocabulary is not especially original. When he calls Democrats “radical left,” “Marxists,” or “hardcore godless communists,” he recycles one of the oldest weapons in American political life: the charge that political opponents are not merely wrong but fundamentally un-American because of their alleged leftist ideology. In his rambling social media posts and ham-fisted rants, Trump uses anti-communism as a blunt political instrument. He labels proposals for expanded health care, rent control, stronger unions, and higher taxes on the wealthy as evidence of some sort of communist conspiracy. articles.title: Public Ownership of Key Economic Sectors Is Popular
articles.author: Chance Phillips
articles.content_excerpt: Democratic voters overwhelmingly support the public ownership and operation of several key industries. At least one of the Democratic politicians who want to win the party’s next presidential primary should take note. A poll I recently commissioned from the Center for Strategic Politics found that a supermajority of Democratic voters support public ownership and operation of health care and the electrical grid. A slight majority supports public ownership of the nation’s railroads. And far more voters said they would support public ownership and operation of artificial intelligence than opposed it. articles.title: Harold Cruse, the Loneliest Black Radical Intellectual
articles.author: Alan Wald
articles.content_excerpt: Harold Wright Cruse (1916–2005), my colleague at the University of Michigan for decades, may have been the most flamboyantly paradoxical radical intellectual ever to roam our institution’s halls. An astonishing autodidact with a wealth of knowledge about cultural and political history, Cruse authored a foundational work in black studies: The Crisis of the Negro Intellectual: A Historical Analysis of the Failure of Black Leadership (1967). Now, two decades after his death, a short, pacy biography by Villanova University theologian and Africana studies scholar Vincent W. Lloyd titled Harold Cruse: Critic, Writer, Teacher captures many of Cruse’s idiosyncrasies to present a riot of contradictions. Charles Booker lost bids for the U.S. Senate in 2020 and 2022. “I didn't think I would ever run again,” Kentucky's Democratic Senate hopeful told about 100 supporters who gathered in front of Paducah’s historic old Hotel Metropolitan. “This is Rocky 3 for me.” The crowd laughed, cheered and waved Booker-for-Senate 2026 signs appreciatively. A 42-year-old former state lawmaker from Louisville, his hometown, Booker is the first African American to win a major party nomination for the Senate in Kentucky. articles.title: Hold Trump Accountable
articles.author: Bill Blum
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. It’s not enough for the Democrats to win the midterms. Whether they take back one or both chambers of Congress, their overriding objective must be to cripple the remainder of Donald Trump ’s presidency and dismantle the MAGA movement he leads. Holding Trump and his key enablers to account for their lawlessness and corruption will be the standard for success. Without accountability, there will be no justice and no end to the growing threat of fascism in America. Of all the accountability tools that will be available should the Democrats prevail on Nov. 3, impeachment and court reform stand out as the most powerful. articles.author: Alan Minsky
articles.content_excerpt: The opinions expressed here are solely the author's and do not reflect the opinions or beliefs of the LA Progressive. LA Progressive has updated its Progressive Voter Guide for California’s 51st Assembly District, replacing Rick Chavez Zbur with Colin Hernandez. A reader recently asked us to revisit this race, pointing to a contradiction between our publication’s defense of free expression and Zbur’s role as a lead author of Assembly Bill 715. That request deserved a serious response. Our voter guide is intended to help readers make informed choices. When readers raise substantive concerns about its contents, we have a responsibility to examine them—and to make changes when the evidence warrants it.
